issue.body:
### What happened?

```
#map = affine_map<(d0, d1, d2) -> (d0, d1, 0)>
#map1 = affine_map<(d0, d1, d2) -> ()>
#map2 = affine_map<(d0, d1, d2) -> (d0, d1, d2)>
module {
  func.func @forward(%arg0: tensor<2x4096x1xf16>) -> tensor<2x4096x1xf16> {
    %cst = arith.constant 1.000000e-05 : f64
    %0 = tensor.empty() : tensor<2x4096x1xf16>
    %1 = tensor.empty() : tensor<f16>
    %2 = linalg.fill ins(%cst : f64) outs(%1 : tensor<f16>) -> tensor<f16>
    %3 = linalg.generic {indexing_maps = [#map, #map1, #map2], iterator_types = ["parallel", "parallel", "parallel"]} ins(%arg0, %2 : tensor<2x4096x1xf16>, tensor<f16>) outs(%0 : tensor<2x4096x1xf16>) {
    ^bb0(%in: f16, %in_0: f16, %out: f16):
      %4 = arith.addf %in, %in_0 : f16
      linalg.yield %4 : f16
    } -> tensor<2x4096x1xf16>
    return %3 : tensor<2x4096x1xf16>
  }
}
```
Since the `linalg.fill` supports casting of the value operand, promoting it to the same data type as the output. This should be a legal IR.
Due to some optimization pass, I think the 0d tensor is somehow promoted to a scalar and this results in an error.
https://mlir.llvm.org/docs/Dialects/Linalg/#linalgfill-mlirlinalgfillop

More info: The fail is happening in the fusion of tensor ops pass.

```
// -----// IR Dump After FusionOfTensorOps Failed (iree-flow-fusion-of-tensor-ops) //----- //
"func.func"() ({
^bb0(%arg0: !hal.buffer_view):
  **%0 = "arith.constant"() {value = 9.99999974E-6 : f32} : () -> f32**
  %1 = "hal.tensor.import"(%arg0) {operand_segment_sizes = array<i32: 1, 0, 0>, target_encoding = tensor<2x4096x1xf16>} : (!hal.buffer_view) -> tensor<2x4096x1xf16>
  %2 = "tensor.empty"() : () -> tensor<2x4096x1xf16>
  %3 = "linalg.generic"(%1, %2) ({
  ^bb0(%arg1: f16, %arg2: f16):
    **%5 = "arith.addf"(%arg1, %0) : (f16, f32) -> f16**
    "linalg.yield"(%5) : (f16) -> ()
  }) {indexing_maps = [affine_map<(d0, d1, d2) -> (d0, d1, d2)>, affine_map<(d0, d1, d2) -> (d0, d1, d2)>], iterator_types = ["parallel", "parallel", "parallel"], operand_segment_sizes = array<i32: 1, 1>} : (tensor<2x4096x1xf16>, tensor<2x4096x1xf16>) -> tensor<2x4096x1xf16>
  %4 = "hal.tensor.export"(%3) {operand_segment_sizes = array<i32: 1, 0, 0>, source_encoding = tensor<2x4096x1xf16>} : (tensor<2x4096x1xf16>) -> !hal.buffer_view
  "func.return"(%4) : (!hal.buffer_view) -> ()
}) {function_type = (!hal.buffer_view) -> !hal.buffer_view, iree.abi.stub, sym_name = "forward"} : () -> ()
```

### Steps to reproduce your issue

cuda-backend
`iree-compile  --iree-input-type=none --iree-vm-bytecode-module-output-format=flatbuffer-binary --iree-hal-target-backends=cuda  --mlir-print-debuginfo --mlir-print-op-on-diagnostic=false --iree-llvm-target-cpu-features=host --iree-hal-cuda-disable-loop-nounroll-wa --iree-stream-resource-index-bits=64 --iree-vm-target-index-bits=64 --iree-util-zero-fill-elided-attrs ~/test_cleaned.mlir`

vulkan-backend
` iree-compile   --iree-input-type=none --iree-vm-bytecode-module-output-format=flatbuffer-binary --iree-hal-target-backends=vulkan --mlir-print-debuginfo --mlir-print-op-on-diagnostic=false --iree-llvm-target-cpu-features=host -iree-vulkan-target-triple=rdna2-unknown-linux --iree-stream-resource-index-bits=64 --iree-vm-target-index-bits=64 --iree-util-zero-fill-elided-attrs ~/test_cleaned.mlir`

This gives 
```
error: 'arith.addf' op requires the same type for all operands and results
      %4 = arith.addf %in, %in_0 : f16
           ^
```
